content: Between 2020 and 2023, the sector experienced a rapid acceleration in technological integration, with the adoption rate of these systems demonstrating a consistent and robust upward trajectory. Specifically, the adoption rate stood at a baseline of 45.0 percent in 2020 and surged to a maximum value of 85.0 percent by the end of 2023. Earlier research and conceptual models, such as the introduction of the "Data Mule" concept in 2004 for underground fuel station monitoring utilizing wireless LoRa technology, served as vital historical benchmarks for the industry [35] . However, these early iterations do not fully capture the profound technological leaps that have characterized the market in recent years [35] . The contemporary focus has decisively shifted away from isolated hardware installations toward the seamless convergence of advanced technologies, notably the integration of Internet of Things enabled sensors and artificial intelligence algorithms designed for sophisticated predictive analysis [27] . As of mid-2026, leading fuel management systems deployed within the South African mining landscape are characterized by their emphasis on real-time data analytics and holistic fleet integration. A prominent example of this technological evolution is Technoton's advanced telematics solution, which provides comprehensive, real-time monitoring of both fuel consumption metrics and critical engine performance parameters across heavy mining equipment [31] . By continuously harvesting and analyzing granular data streams, this solution empowers mine operators to immediately identify operational inefficiencies, unauthorized fuel siphoning, or mechanical anomalies [31] . Industry analyses, such as those detailing artificial intelligence tools anticipated to revolutionize mining operations in 2026, align closely with the broader trend of technological convergence [34] . While some of these insights remain general in scope and occasionally lack specific technical schematics regarding fuel tracking applications, the underlying premise is clear: predictive algorithms are becoming indispensable for anticipating fuel demand, routing fuel delivery vehicles efficiently across expansive mine sites, and identifying complex consumption patterns that human analysts might overlook [34] . It is crucial to contextualize these technological advancements within the broader economic realities facing the South African mining sector.
